summary: 21 findings checked (9 logic, 12 interface): 19 confirmed, 2 refuted, none unclear. High (a pad player meets a wrong result in normal play): chord-plain-after-modifier-release, held-button-leaks-into-flight-after-close, focus-mark-wiped-by-rerender, b-closes-station-while-docked. Medium (unusual device or sequence): lever-lost-while-panel-open-and-no-end-stop, pad-only-cannot-cancel-listening, menu-button-can-be-given-away, bindings-in-pause-menu-opens-unfocused, number-field-needs-keyboard, phantom-held-button-blocks-assignment. Low: corrupt-pad-settings-kill-loop (no writer in the app produces such a save), second-pad-press-not-reported, lever-two-pads-same-dev, mouse-click-and-wheel-live-in-pad-mode, aim-sum-exceeds-server-cap, axis-assigned-to-two-actions, keys-named-directly-in-pad-texts, german-ui-shows-english-pad-labels, docs-and-report-claim-more-than-checked. Refuted as defects (the behaviour is real, it is the design, and the obvious repair would do harm): pad-analog-live-while-device-keys, axis-half-ignores-modifier. Merges: the 'Esc cancels.' part of keys-named-directly-in-pad-texts went into pad-only-cannot-cancel-listening; menu-button-can-be-given-away and the button half of pad-only-cannot-cancel-listening share one fix (binds.ts guard); the two focus findings have different causes and stay apart. Reviewer statements corrected: Y+View that opens the map does not toggle cruise (the panel gate swallows it), only the one that closes it does; Y+Menu that opens the system map closes it again at once; the server clamps an aim above 0.5, it does not reject it; a numeric string as turn rate works; the 844 x 390 sentence of CLIENT.md holds for the pause menu in a run with today's ui.css (the report it contradicts is from 09:38, before the CSS changed); after the Menu button is given away the binding screen is still reachable by pad from the start screen after a reload. How it was checked (all under assets/audio/cache/review/verify-pad/, ignored by git): pure.ts (npx tsx: readPads, captureProgress, assignPad, assignAxis), input.ts (npx tsx: the real Input class with stubbed browser globals and the panel logic of Game.ts 916-935), entry.tsx bundled with esbuild and driven by driver.mjs, driver2.mjs, driver3*.mjs in headless Chromium with a fake navigator.getGamepads (real StartScreen, PauseMenu, Bindings, PadNav, Input and ui.css; pages served by request interception on a made-up origin, so no server and no port), patch.mjs and fixcheck.ts (patched copies of gamepad.ts and Input.ts in the scratch folder: the fixes for the chord order, the held button, the lever, the mouse in pad mode and the aim cap were run there and pass, the chord fix in its narrow form, which mutes only a button pressed while the modifier is held, so that fire or thrust held from before comes back after a chord; only the existing test gamepad.test.ts 124-129, which asserts the old release order, fails and has to be rewritten), entry2.tsx and driver4.mjs (a key on a component root makes Preact build a new node). Not verified: anything on real hardware; the real Station component (a stand-in with its tab row and number field was used); select and galaxy map by pad; whether a browser lets the scripted click on the licence link open a tab; fixes marked 'Not run'. Seen on the way, in neither list: (1) with no pointer lock, a key pressed while a stick is held sets the device to keys and the stick's thrust drops from [0,0,1] to [0,0,0] until the stick has been at rest once (input.ts section 3); (2) while docked, the Menu button and opening a map also remove the station screen, with the same dead end as B; (3) after the binding screen is opened from the pause menu the first press marked 'Reset to defaults' at 1600 x 900. Nothing in the repository was changed except this report; the reviewed files had the same modification times at 16:04 as when first read; no server was started and no port used.

verdicts.claim: Releasing the chord modifier (Y) before the target button switches the target's plain binding on, so a chord can also run the target's own action. The same gap makes a held button fire a second time when Y is tapped while it is down.
verdicts.proof: Run, pure and through the real Input class. verify-pad/pure.ts section 1 (readPads): Y, Y+View, then View alone gives pressed=cruise; likewise Menu (menu), RT (firePrimary), A (thrustUp), D-pad up (targetAhead), LB (rollLeft). verify-pad/input.ts section 1 (Input.pollPads plus the panel logic of Game.ts 916-935): Y+RT then Y up gives buttons=1, the ship fires; Y+A gives thrust [0,1,0]; Y+B gives flight assist off and thrust [0,-1,0]; Y+X gives fold and buttons=32 (tool); Y+L3 gives silent running and boost; Y+D-pad up gives power to engines, then 'targetAhead RUNS'. Panels change two cases: Y+View that opens the map has its cruise swallowed by the panel gate (Input.ts 233), Y+View that closes the map gives 'cruise RUNS'; Y+Menu that opens the system map is followed by menu, which closes it again (panel=null), and Y+Menu that closes it opens the pause menu (panel=menu). Reverse overlap: View held and Y tapped gives 'cruise RUNS' twice. Cause: gamepad.ts 380, isOn = down && !modHeld && !mods.has(n), with no memory that the button was down together with the modifier. gamepad.test.ts 124-129 ('lets the plain binding work again once the modifier is released') asserts this order as wanted. A 60 Hz poll sees the in-between state whenever the two releases are a frame apart; how often that is in play was not measured (my estimate: about every second chord).
verdicts.fix: gamepad.ts readPads, two small rules. (1) Add muted: Set<string> (keys '<pad index>|<button>') to PadState and emptyPadState; after modHeld is computed, a button that is down is muted when before.muted has it, or when it went down in this reading while a modifier is held (modHeld && !was?.[n]); in the plain branch (line 380) also require that muted lacks the key; return muted in state. A button pressed during a chord then stays silent until it is released, whichever of the two is let go first. (2) Report a plain binding as pressed only with its button's own going down: collect a set 'fresh' in the entries loop (button: !was?.[k.n]; chord and axis half: !before.on.has(key)) and push to pressed only actions that are new in held and in fresh. A button held from before the modifier (fire, thrust, roll) still pauses during the chord and comes back when the modifier is let go, as today, but a single-press action no longer runs a second time. Do not mute every button that is down while a modifier is held: held fire or thrust would then not come back after a chord. Run on a patched copy (verify-pad/patch.mjs, fixcheck.ts): the sequences above stay silent and the next lone press fires; RT held through Y + D-pad right fires again afterwards; A held with Y tapped thrusts again with no new press reported; View held with Y tapped runs cruise once; every default binding still fires; of the existing chord tests only gamepad.test.ts 124-129 fails. Tests: rewrite 124-129 to expect thrustUp off after [3,0] then [0] and on after [] then [0]; add [3],[3,8],[8] expecting pressed without cruise; [8],[8,3],[8] expecting pressed empty in the third reading; [0],[0,3],[0] expecting thrustUp held again; [7],[7,3],[7,3,15],[7,3],[7] expecting firePrimary held at the end; in input.test.ts Y+RT then Y up expecting sample().buttons & 1 to be 0.

verdicts.claim: loadSettings lets malformed pad.axes entries and a non-numeric pad.turnRate through. readPads then throws on every poll and the first throw ends Input's animation-frame loop; a partial entry yields NaN; a non-numeric turn rate sends aim [NaN, NaN].
verdicts.proof: Run (verify-pad/input.ts section 2, pure.ts section 2). After loadSettings with axes.yaw=[null] or an object, pollPads throws ('Cannot read properties of null (reading dev)', 'object is not iterable'); with the loop driven by hand: frames run=1, callbacks left=0, and RT held afterwards gives buttons=0. Entry without deadzone and curve: shapeAxis gives NaN, yaw stays 0 at full deflection, active=true at rest. turnRate 'fast': aim [NaN,NaN], on the wire [null,null], which the server drops as a whole input (validate.ts 14-15 and 87). Narrower than claimed: turnRate '0.5' works (coerced, aim 0.01333); pad=null and pad.axes=null are handled; the menu loop of padnav keeps running, though store.device never becomes pad and so its mark stays hidden. Reachability: no writer in the app produces such an entry (assignAxis, patchAxis, joystickPreset and the defaults write complete entries; the shape of PadAxisBinding is unchanged since its first commit 1fdf63a), so it takes a hand edit, a foreign build or a later change of the shape. Hence low.
verdicts.fix: store.ts loadSettings: build pad through a small cleaner in place of the spread at line 264: turnRate a finite number clamped to 0.2..1, else 1; per axis action keep only array entries that are objects with a string dev and a whole axis >= 0, and fill invert (boolean), deadzone and curve (finite, else 0.12 and 1.6) and lever (boolean). Input.ts startPadLoop: wrap pollPads in try/catch (log once) so that one bad frame cannot end the loop. Not run. Test (input.test.ts, 'settings with pad codes'): store0 with pad {turnRate:'fast', axes:{yaw:[null], pitch:{dev:'std',axis:3}, roll:[{dev:'std',axis:0}]}}, loadSettings, then expect pollPads not to throw, turnRate 1, roll[0].deadzone to be a number, and readPads at rest to give active=false.

verdicts.claim: Pad axes and held pad buttons count in sample() whenever the controls are live, whichever device was used last. That part is true; that it is a defect is not.
verdicts.proof: Run (verify-pad/input.ts section 3): device keys, pointer locked, a pad resting at 0.2 on all four axes gives thrust [0.0216, 0, -0.0216] and yaw 0.0173 rad/s (0.99 deg/s). So the behaviour exists, and it is the design: CLIENT.md 45-46 says pads feed the same input values as keyboard and mouse; store.device decides only the hints and whether pointer lock is needed (Input.ts 103-107); a rest offset above the dead zone does the same in pad mode, where the dead zone slider of the binding screen is the remedy. Gating the axes on store.device would break stick plus keyboard: every keydown sets keys (Input.ts 341) and only a fresh press or a stick that leaves rest sets pad again (223). The same run shows that this cost already exists where there is no pointer lock: stick held forward, a key pressed, thrust falls from [0,0,1] to [0,0,0] until the stick has been at rest. The scenario also needs a pad with more than 0.12 rest offset that was touched in this page session, since browsers show a pad only after a button press.
verdicts.fix: None. Do not gate analog input on store.device. If the drift of an idle pad ever matters, raise the default dead zone or say in CLIENT.md that a connected pad always counts.

verdicts.claim: A lever move made while a panel is open is never applied, and the lever can rest up to 0.02 short of zero or full.
verdicts.proof: Run with the real Input (verify-pad/input.ts section 4): lever at 0.2, moved to 0.8 while the map is open, map closed: throttle stays 0.200; a nudge to 0.81 changes nothing, 0.83 gives 0.830. End stops: path 0.5 > 0.3 > 0.12 > 0.05 > 0.035 > 0.018 > 0.006 > 0 ends at throttle 0.0180; path 0.5 > 0.2 > 0.019 > 0.01 > 0 at 0.0190; path 0.5 > 0.981 > 0.99 > 1 at 0.9810. Cause: Input.ts 241-243 moves lastLever before asking active(), and takes over only on a difference above 0.02. Needs a device with an axis bound as throttle lever, which no default has; hence medium.
verdicts.fix: Input.ts pollPads, lever block (237-244): snap the position to 0 below LEVER_TAKEOVER and to 1 above 1 - LEVER_TAKEOVER; move lastLever and the throttle only while active(), when the snapped position differs from lastLever by more than LEVER_TAKEOVER or has reached 0 or 1 and differs from lastLever. Run on a patched copy (fixcheck.ts): the three paths end at exactly 0, 0 and 1; the move made in the panel is applied when the map closes (0.8); the existing test 'lets the lever take over the setpoint only when it moves' still holds. Tests (input.test.ts): those four sequences.

verdicts.claim: 'pressed' comes from the union of held actions, so a press on a second device of a single-press action that another device already holds is not reported.
verdicts.proof: Run (verify-pad/pure.ts section 5): pad 0 holds View (pressed=cruise); pad 1 presses View too: pressed empty; pad 0 releases while pad 1 holds: pressed empty. Cause: gamepad.ts 422-423. It needs two devices holding the same single-press action at the same moment, and one pilot loses nothing by it; hence low.
verdicts.fix: gamepad.ts readPads: collect pressed per binding key, not per action: in the entries loop, when isOn and before.on lacks the key, add e.action to a set and return that set as pressed (released stays as it is). Not run. Test (gamepad.test.ts): two standard pads, pad 0 holds View, then pad 1 presses View: pressed equals ['cruise'].

verdicts.claim: When a lever binding's dev matches more than one connected device, the lever value is that of the last matching device in the list; the other lever is ignored.
verdicts.proof: Run (verify-pad/pure.ts section 6): lever on std axis 3, pad 0 at -1 and pad 1 at 0.5 gives lever 0.75; swapped gives 0; pad 0 at full with pad 1 idle gives 0.5. gamepad.ts 407-408 overwrites lever for every match. With one device per key (a stick beside a standard pad) the value is right (lever 1 in the same run). Needs two devices on one dev: two standard pads, or two identical units, which share a device key by design (gamepad.ts 78).
verdicts.fix: gamepad.ts readPads: follow the lever that moved last. Add leverOwner (the '<pad index>|<axis>' key) to PadState; a matching lever that moved by more than LEVER_MOVE since the last reading becomes the owner; lever is the owner's value, or the first match while there is no owner or it is gone. Not run. Test (gamepad.test.ts): two pads on one dev; pad 0 moves and lever follows it while pad 1 rests; then pad 1 moves and lever follows that.

verdicts.claim: An axis half bound as a button is not silenced while a chord modifier is held. The observation is true; the wrong result claimed does not exist.
verdicts.proof: Run (verify-pad/pure.ts section 7): with 'Pad:std:a2+' bound and Y held, axis 2 at 0.9 gives held=camera. The wrong result claimed, the plain action firing together with a chord on the same control, has no path: a chord is two buttons (parsePadCode, gamepad.ts 128-129), and captureProgress scans only buttons once a modifier is pending (483-489), so no chord can have an axis as its target. The silence rule exists so that a chord's target does not also run its plain action, and the comment at gamepad.ts 368 names 'this device's other buttons'. An axis half that keeps working while Y is held matches the analog axes, which are not silenced either.
verdicts.fix: None needed. If one rule for all plain bindings is wanted, require !modHeld in the axis branch too (gamepad.ts 387-388); that is a design choice, not a repair.

verdicts.claim: While the device is pad, a mouse click or wheel turn made without moving the mouse acts on the ship although the pointer is not captured.
verdicts.proof: Run with the real Input (verify-pad/input.ts section 8): device pad, pointer not locked, a mousedown without mouse movement gives buttons=1 (the primary weapon fires while the button is down); one wheel notch gives throttle 0.1; the same two with device keys give nothing, as before controller support. Path: active() is true without pointer lock in pad mode (Input.ts 103-107); onButton (360) and the wheel handler (78) ask only active(); only mousemove and keydown set the device back to keys (74, 341). It needs a click or wheel turn with no mouse movement since the last pad input; hence low.
verdicts.fix: Input.ts: set store.device.value = 'keys' at the top of onButton when down, and at the top of the wheel handler, before active() is asked. Run on a patched copy (fixcheck.ts): click and wheel switch to keys and do nothing without pointer lock; under pointer lock the click fires as before. Test (input.test.ts, with a window stub that keeps its listeners): device pad, no lock, call the mousedown listener, expect device keys and sample().buttons & 1 to be 0.

verdicts.claim: The aim sent is the capped mouse part plus the uncapped stick part and can exceed the 0.5 rad per tick the server accepts. The server clamps it; it does not reject it.
verdicts.proof: Run (verify-pad/input.ts section 9): right stick full and a mouse turn of 2.2 rad give aim[0]=0.52667 in two ticks in a row. Server: validate.ts 14-15 clamps into the range given at line 83, so 0.027 rad of stick turn is dropped in such a tick and the client's own prediction differs by that much until the next snapshot. Only while a flick of more than 0.47 rad per tick and a deflected stick coincide.
verdicts.fix: Input.ts sample(): give the mouse the room the stick leaves: ax = clamp(this.aimX, -AIM_PER_TICK - px, AIM_PER_TICK - px), and the same for ay; the carry into the next tick stays as it is. Run on a patched copy (fixcheck.ts): largest tick 0.50000, and the total equals mouse 1.1 plus the stick part, nothing lost. Test (input.test.ts): addMouse(500, 0) with the right stick at 1, four samples: each aim[0] <= 0.5 and their sum equals 500 * sensitivity + 4 * rate * dt.

verdicts.claim: The focus mark is a class added by hand; when Preact rewrites the class attribute of the marked element the mark is gone while that element is still the one A acts on.
verdicts.proof: Run in headless Chromium with the real StartScreen, Bindings, PadNav and ui.css (verify-pad/entry.tsx, driver.mjs). A on the Settings tab of the start screen: the count of '.padfocus' goes from 1 to 0 while PadNav.current is still that button (class 'on'); a second A, with nothing marked, closed the tab again. With the mark on the open tab (class 'on padfocus'), LB: count 0, current still the old tab (class ''). A on Assign in the binding screen: count 0, current is the same button, now 'Cancel' with class 'on'. A stand-in panel with the tab row of Station.tsx 227-228 copied: it opens with the first tab marked, RB: count 0 (the real Station was not mounted). The element keeps the real focus, so in this Chromium the outline falls back from 2 px amber (ui.css 297) to the 1 px cyan :focus-visible line (ui.css 51), which ui.css 296 itself calls unreliable. Cause: set() (padnav.ts 272-276) adds the class once, and Preact writes the whole class attribute when the element's own class value changes. Met at the first RB after docking.
verdicts.fix: padnav.ts PadNav.poll, right after the container block (line 247): put the mark back when it is missing: if (this.current?.isConnected && !this.current.classList.contains(MARK)) this.current.classList.add(MARK); Not run. There is no DOM test of PadNav, so the browser check has to catch it: in scripts/pad-check.mjs stationByPad after tap(page, B.RB) (line 170) check that focus(page) is not null, and in flight() after 'A on assign starts listening' (line 323) check the same.

verdicts.claim: While the binding screen listens, only Escape or a mouse click cancels; the pad cannot, and the text shown tells the pad user to press Esc. (Includes the 'Esc cancels.' part of keys-named-directly-in-pad-texts.)
verdicts.proof: Run with the real Bindings screen (verify-pad/driver.mjs S3). Button mode on 'Cruise drive', text shown: 'Press a button. Hold one and press another for a combination. Esc cancels.'; B pressed to cancel: listening ends with cruise=[KeyJ, Pad:std:b1], thrustDown=[ControlLeft, KeyC], padCleared=[thrustDown], so B was taken from thrust down. Axis mode on yaw, text 'Move the axis all the way. Esc cancels.': B, Menu, A and D-pad down each leave it listening with the panel unchanged, and it is still listening 4 s later; pushing the left stick ended it with yaw on axis 0, which thrustX also uses, and the right stick no longer yaws. Paths: Bindings.tsx 54-59 (Escape only), 81-87 (the axis mode takes only an axis), padnav.ts 249 (mute while capturing), Input.ts 232. On a device with only a pad, which CLIENT.md 46-47 names as the only way to play on a phone or tablet, there is no way out without changing a binding.
verdicts.fix: Bindings.tsx step(): in axis mode end listening when captureNext returns a button, so any button cancels. In button mode the guard proposed under menu-button-can-be-given-away makes the pause-menu button the cancel: its assignment is refused and listening ends with nothing changed. Texts en.ts 383-384 and de.ts 385-386: name the pad way, for example '{MENU} or Esc cancels.' with the label of the menu action's pad code and 'Any button or Esc cancels.' ('{MENU} oder Esc bricht ab.', 'Eine beliebige Taste oder Esc bricht ab.'). Not run. Test (scripts/pad-check.mjs): start listening on an axis, tap B, check that '.bindings .listen' is gone and settings.pad.axes is unchanged; start listening on a button, tap Menu, check that the bindings are unchanged.

verdicts.claim: The button that opens the pause menu can be assigned to another action; the menu action is then left without a controller code and the pause menu cannot be opened from the pad in flight.
verdicts.proof: Run. verify-pad/pure.ts section 13: assignPad(defaults, 'cruise', 'Pad:std:b9') gives menu=[Escape], padCleared=[menu], and Menu then reports pressed=cruise. Through the real screen (driver.mjs S13): Menu pressed while 'Camera' listens gives camera=[KeyV, Pad:std:b9], menu=[Escape], the menu row shows an en dash; back in flight Menu gives actions=[camera] and panel=null. Qualification of 'cannot reach the binding screen': after a page reload the start screen reaches Settings, Controller assignments and 'Reset to defaults' by pad (driver.mjs S2b reached that button with the D-pad). The likely way into this is the missing cancel: a pad user who wants out of listening presses Menu or B.
verdicts.fix: binds.ts assignPad: do not take the last controller code from 'menu': if action is not 'menu' and code is the only pad code in s.bindings.menu, return s unchanged. clearPad(s, 'menu') returns s as well (or the Clear button of that row is disabled, Bindings.tsx 155). The menu action itself can still be given another button. Not run. Test (input.test.ts 'binding edits'): assignPad(base(), 'cruise', 'Pad:std:b9') leaves 'Pad:std:b9' on menu and cruise as it was; clearPad(base(), 'menu') keeps it; assignPad(base(), 'menu', 'Pad:std:b16') still works.

verdicts.claim: B in the station panel closes it while docked and nothing reopens it; market and services stay out of reach until the pilot undocks and docks again. Not specific to B.
verdicts.proof: Path named, the pad part run. padnav.ts back() 345-356: the station panel has no data-padback (only Bindings.tsx 113 has one) and the phase is playing, so B sets store.panel to null. Run on the stand-in station panel with the real PadNav (verify-pad/driver2.mjs a): panel 'station' before B, null after. The only code that opens the station panel is ui/index.tsx 25, on the change from not docked to docked (grep of 'panel.value =' and 'togglePanel(' over client/src finds nothing else outside dev/). Afterwards the HUD shows only 'DOCKED' (Hud.tsx 524-525), the Menu button opens the pause menu and the dock chord undocks (Game.ts 938). Escape did the same before controller support, and the pad's Menu button (Game.ts 921) and opening a map while docked (togglePanel replaces the panel) end in the same place. index.tsx 20-21 says closing is intended; the defect is that nothing brings the screen back. The real Station component was not mounted.
verdicts.fix: Give the docked pilot a way back that every device has: Menu.tsx PauseMenu, in the header beside Resume, a button shown while store.station.value is not null that sets store.panel.value = 'station' (new text key, en 'Station services', de 'Stationsdienste'). By pad: Menu, then A on it. Optional on top: padnav.ts back() does nothing on the station panel, so that B cannot close it by accident. Not run. Test (scripts/pad-check.mjs stationByPad, before the undock): tap B, check that the panel is gone, tap Menu, navTo that button, tap A, check that '.backdrop .panel nav.tabs' is back.

verdicts.claim: A button that is still down when it has closed a panel flies the ship until it is released: A thrusts up, B thrusts down. The same holds for a stick still deflected.
verdicts.proof: Run. Real Input (verify-pad/input.ts section 10): pause menu open with A down gives thrust [0,0,0]; the panel closes while A is held: thrust [0,1,0] until release; B likewise [0,-1,0]; a left stick still pushed when the panel closes gives [0,0,-1]. The whole chain in the browser harness with the real PauseMenu, PadNav and Input (driver2.mjs b): A held 150 ms on Resume: panel=null, active()=true, thrust [0,1,0]; B held to close: [0,-1,0]. Cause: Input.ts 216-219 fill padHeld and padAxes every frame, 232-233 hold back only single presses, and sample() (139-140) uses them as soon as the panel is gone. A is thrust up, which lifts a landed ship off (text ctl.land). Met at every panel closed with A or B.
verdicts.fix: Input.ts pollPads: a button that was down while a menu or panel had the pad stays silent until it is let go. Keep padStale (a set of actions) and wasBlocked; blocked = the phase is not playing or a panel is open; when blocked or wasBlocked, padStale = new Set(r.held), otherwise drop from padStale what r.held no longer has; padHeld = r.held without padStale. Tie it to the panel and not to active(), so that the first pad press after mouse use is not swallowed. A side effect to accept: a button held right through a panel that opens and closes, or through a fold handoff (phase not playing), also needs a new press, for example RT held across Y+LB for the contacts. Run on a patched copy (fixcheck.ts): no thrust after A or B closed a panel, also when the panel closes in the very frame the button goes down; a new press works; RT in flight, and RT as the press that takes the device over from the mouse, fire at once. Optional: the same for the axes (zero until the sticks have been at rest once). Test (input.test.ts): panel 'menu', pads=[pad([0])], pollPads, panel=null, pollPads, expect sample().thrust[1] to be 0; release and press again, expect 1; and the variant in which panel=null is set before the poll that first sees the button.

verdicts.claim: Opening the binding screen from the pause menu, and going back, reuses the same panel node, so PadNav sets no focus: nothing is marked and the first press only marks a control.
verdicts.proof: Run with the real PauseMenu and Bindings (verify-pad/driver.mjs S2): after A on 'Controller assignments' the panel is the same DOM node (class now 'panel wide'), the count of '.padfocus' is 0 and PadNav.current is the removed button (not in the page). The next A only marked a control, and at 1600 x 900 that control was 'Reset to defaults', chosen as the nearest to where the old button stood (padnav.ts 307-309); one more A would reset every assignment. B back to the pause menu: same node again, no mark. From the start screen (S2b) the same screen opens with 'Back' marked at once, because there a form gives way to a div and a new node is built. Cause: padnav.ts 241-247 compares the container by identity; Menu.tsx 168-176 returns a div in the place of a div.
verdicts.fix: Menu.tsx PauseMenu: give the two roots different keys (key 'bindings' on the 'panel wide' div, key 'menu' on the 'panel narrow' div), so that Preact builds a new node and PadNav's container check sets the initial focus as on the start screen. The mechanism was run (verify-pad/entry2.tsx, driver4.mjs): without keys the same node, with keys a new one. Test (scripts/pad-check.mjs flight()): after waitFor('.bindings') check that focus(page) is not null and is the Back button, before navTo, which today presses Down when nothing is marked and so hides this.

verdicts.claim: assignAxis replaces only the binding of the action being assigned, so one physical axis can drive two actions, where a button is taken from its old owner.
verdicts.proof: Run (verify-pad/pure.ts section 14): assignAxis(defaults, 'pitch', 'std', 1) leaves thrustZ on std axis 1 as well; left stick forward then gives pitch 1 and thrustZ 1. Seen through the screen too (driver.mjs S3): yaw assigned to axis 0 while thrustX keeps axis 0. binds.ts 45-51 filters only the list of the action; assignPad (25-36) removes a code from every other action.
verdicts.fix: binds.ts assignAxis: remove a binding with the same dev and axis from the lists of the other actions, as assignPad does for buttons. Not run. Test (input.test.ts 'binding edits'): assignAxis(DEFAULT_PAD_SETTINGS, 'pitch', 'std', 1) leaves no std axis 1 under thrustZ.

verdicts.claim: Narrowed to one part: the pad help block names the default button positions, not the current bindings. The 'Esc cancels.' part is merged into pad-only-cannot-cancel-listening; the chat placeholder is not a defect.
verdicts.proof: Run (verify-pad/driver2.mjs d): with cruise bound to Guide (Pad:std:b16) the help in the pause menu still reads 'View: cruise   Y + X: fold jump ...'. format.ts 55-59 padHelpParams() names buttons 0 to 11 by position and the ctlp.* texts (en.ts 407-412) tie actions to those names, while the HUD hints follow the bindings (bindKey). The chat placeholder (en.ts 189) names Enter and Esc, but chat has no pad binding and needs a keyboard to type, so those are the right keys.
verdicts.fix: Smallest: say what the block is. en.ts 413 and de.ts 415 (ctlp.custom): 'These are the default assignments. Your own are under Settings, Controller.' and 'Das ist die Standardbelegung. Eigene Belegungen findest du unter Einstellungen, Controller.' Fuller: write the ctlp.* lines with one placeholder per action and fill them from the current bindings. verdicts.claim: Pad button and axis labels are English in the German interface and differ from the German help text; the reason for the disabled Joystick preset is only a tooltip.
verdicts.proof: Run (verify-pad/driver2.mjs c) with lang de: the help line says 'Steuerkreuz: Ziel voraus ...' while the binding rows read 'Energie auf Schilde | Y + D-pad left', 'Ziel voraus (sonst nächstes Schiff) | D-pad up', 'Reiseantrieb | View', and the axis rows 'Axis 3', 'Axis 4'. gamepad.ts 143-155 holds 'D-pad up', 'Button n' and 'Axis n' in English. The Joystick preset button is disabled with title 'Schließe zuerst einen Joystick an.'; a disabled button is not focusable by pad (padnav.ts 137), so the reason never shows there.
verdicts.fix: Keep gamepad.ts free of i18n and translate where labels are shown: let padButtonName, padAxisName and padCodeLabel take an optional table of words (D-pad, up, down, left, right, Button, Axis) with the English defaults, and pass t() values from format.ts bindLabel and Bindings.tsx (new keys; de: Steuerkreuz, hoch, runter, links, rechts, Taste, Achse). The short HUD form (D with an arrow) and face names such as View or Cross stay. Bindings.tsx 130: show the reason as text beside the button while no joystick is connected. Not run. Test (gamepad.test.ts): padCodeLabel('Pad:std:b3+b14', 'xbox', German words) is 'Y + Steuerkreuz links'; a generic 'Pad:x:b13' is 'Taste 14'.

verdicts.claim: A number field moves one unit per press or repeat, however long the direction is held; text fields cannot be filled without a keyboard; the licence link is a pad target.
verdicts.proof: Run with the real PadNav on a field like the one at Station.tsx 281 (verify-pad/driver.mjs S1c): activated with A and right held for 3.0 s, the value went from 1 to 22, one unit per repeat; 500 units take 0.35 s + 499 x 0.12 s, about a minute. A slider held as long ran from 1.0 to its end stop 0.2 (driver.mjs S2b): padnav.ts 186 multiplies by 4 after ten repeats, the number branch 201-206 ignores count. The market has no other way to set a quantity (Station.tsx 281: the field alone). Read, not run: activate() only focuses a text field (padnav.ts 327-330) and the interface has no on-screen keyboard, so with no saved name Launch stays disabled (Menu.tsx 146) on a device that has a pad and nothing to type with; FOCUSABLE (128) includes a[href], so A clicks the licence link (target _blank). Whether a browser lets that scripted click open a tab was not run, since Playwright switches the popup blocker off.
verdicts.fix: padnav.ts adjust(), number branch: speed up with count as the slider does, through a pure exported numberStep(count) that returns 1 up to 10 repeats, 10 up to 30 and 100 beyond, multiplied into the step and clamped to min and max. For the name: Menu.tsx 117 starts with a made-up name when none is saved (for example 'Pilot' and four digits), so that Launch works without typing. For the link: leave a[target=_blank] out of FOCUSABLE. Not run. Tests: padnav.test.ts numberStep(1) is 1, numberStep(11) is 10, numberStep(31) is 100; pad-check: hold right 3 s on a quantity field and expect more than 100.

verdicts.claim: Confirmed in part: several controller-menu features that CLIENT.md describes have no step in the browser check, the PadNav class has no test, and one pad-check assertion cannot fail. Refuted in part: the 844 x 390 sentence holds for the pause menu today.
verdicts.proof: Read: scripts/pad-check.mjs has no step for a slider, a select, the repeat of a held direction or the galaxy map list, which CLIENT.md 70-72 describes; padnav.test.ts line 2 imports only the pure helpers; pad-check.mjs 153 asserts f.text === '' where text is the textContent (focus(), line 91), which is '' for every input, so the step cannot tell the server field from the name field. Run, against the claim (verify-pad/driver2.mjs e): at 844 x 390 the real pause menu with today's ui.css lies between y=3 and y=387 of a 390 px viewport, has overflow auto with 789 px of content scrolling inside, and D-pad down brought 'Disconnect' into view (bottom 385). The open issue in pad-ui-report.json was written at 09:38; ui.css last changed at 14:31. The station panel was not rendered; its rule is height min(56em, 94vh) (ui.css 390). The phone pass does run the three start-screen checks of startByPad, but none about fit. The harness runs exercised slider, repeat and number field (they work); select and galaxy map were not run.
verdicts.fix: scripts/pad-check.mjs: let focus() return the element's value and its index among the inputs and assert index 1 at line 153; add steps: left on the field-of-view slider of the pause menu changes settings.fov; right changes a select; D-pad down held for 1 s moves by more than one control; Y+View opens the galaxy map, the D-pad reaches a system button and A selects it; in phone() assert that the panel's rectangle lies inside the viewport. CLIENT.md 79-82: list what the script checks, and count 'the panels fit' as checked once that assertion exists.

verdicts.claim: A button that reads as held on one device when listening starts becomes the pending modifier, and presses on any other device are then never looked at.
verdicts.proof: Run of the pure function (verify-pad/pure.ts section 12): with button 5 of a second device held from the start, captureProgress returns pending {dev 044f-b10a, n 5}; A pressed on the standard pad for three frames and then released: pending unchanged and done=null every time; a second button on the device with the held one gives the chord b5+b2; the axis mode is not affected (the stick axis of the other pad is captured). gamepad.ts 480-490 looks only at the pending device; 493-497 take a button held at the start as the modifier. Bindings.tsx 61-71 (read): after 1.5 s the wait for all buttons to be up gives up and the held button is part of 'before'. With pad input alone the assignment then cannot end (see pad-only-cannot-cancel-listening). Needs a device with a button that reads as held: a latched switch or mode dial of a HOTAS, or a stuck button. Not run on hardware or with two pads in the browser.
verdicts.fix: gamepad.ts captureProgress, in the pending branch before 'return { pending, done: null }': look for a new press on the other devices (captureNext(before, now without the pending device)); if it is a button, make that the pending one. A held button elsewhere then no longer blocks, and a chord on the device with the held button still works. Not run. Test (gamepad.test.ts 'capture'): before = [standard pad idle, stick with b5 down]; the first step gives pending stick b5; with A down on the standard pad pending becomes {std, 0}; with A up done is {button, std, 0}.
